messages.subject: Translation and scaling with semi-landmarks
parts:
Dear goemorph R team:

Thanks to the whole team for your great contribution. It has been very helpful in conducting shape analysis.

I am conducting morphometrics study using geomorph package. I am doing measurements of three superimposition techniques: three steps super imposition, two steps (translation and scaling), and superimposition with semi-landmarks. In the sliding of semi-landmarks, I conducted the general Procrustes analysis (GPA), which is a three steps superimposition. I also want to do the two steps, translation and scaling, superimposition with semi-landmarks. 

Base on what I have read and understood, the semi-landmarks alignment is closely related to the rotation step of the GPA.
Now my question is, can I do the translation and scaling superimposition and sliding of semi-landmarks. If yes, can you suggest how to go about.

Once again, thanks for your work in sharing valuable knowledge and I wait any response,

Cordially,

Angel

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Translation and scaling with semi-landmarks
parts:
Angel,

 

I don’t understand the statement “the semi-landmarks alignment is closely related to the rotation step of GPA”. The sliding of semilandmarks is in fact an additional step embedded within an ‘extended’ GPA algorithm. With fixed landmarks only, one translates, scales, and rotates. A mean shape is found, and the process is repeated against the mean, and this is iterated until convergence. For GPA with sliding landmarks, the algorithm includes translation, scaling, rotation and sliding. This is then iterated numerous times.

 

If one wishes to implement only components of this, one needs to write their own algorithm for it, or adapt an existing one.  Note however that in these cases, this results in major differences in the expected data space that results. Rohlf had a paper in the 1990s describing the different dataspaces from translation only, translation and scaling, translation, rotation scaling, etc. Each has consequences, not just as ‘a procedure’, but also in terms of what one expects in terms of patterns in data. Statistical shape theory is only valid for fully superimposed shapes: it does not apply to data in say, form space, pre-shape spaces, ‘fibers’ in pre-shape space, etc.

 

Dean

 

Dr. Dean C. Adams

Director of Graduate Education, EEB Program

Professor

Department of Ecology, Evolution, and Organismal Biology

Dear Dr. Adams:

Thank you, you answered my query and please ignore the statement. Thanks also for the explanation on implementing GPA and for suggesting the reference; I got two papaers of the same year, may you confirm which one:
1. Rohlf, F.J.  1990.  Morphometrics.  Annual Reviews of Ecology and Systematics 21:299-316.
2. Rohlf, F.J. and D. Slice.  1990.  Extension of the Procrustes method for the optimal superimposition of landmarks.  Systematic Zoology 39: 40-59.

In so doing, I'm learning about geometric morphometrics. I know implementing different techniques of superimposition will have consequences on the patterns and interpretation of the data. 

 I am new in R and I cannot deuce the sliding step from getAnywhere('gpagen'); can you provide me the algorithm for doing only the sliding and I can try to develop for the different GPA steps needed.

Cordially,

Angel

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Translation and scaling with semi-landmarks
parts:
Angel,

To define sliding landmarks, one must input a “curves” matrix for 2D data or a “surfaces” vector for surface sliding semilandmarks for 3D data.  These are arguments found in the gpagen help file.

Admittedly, we should do a better job in the help file to indicate that one can use “define.sliders”, a function to set up the curves matrix.  We will update that.  But if you look at the define.sliders help file, you should get the help you need.

Best,
Mike

Thanks to the whole team for your great contribution. It has been very helpful in conducting shape analysis.

 

I am conducting morphometrics study using geomorph package. I am doing measurements of three superimposition techniques: three steps super imposition, two steps (translation and scaling), and superimposition with semi-landmarks. In the sliding of semi-landmarks, I conducted the general Procrustes analysis (GPA), which is a three steps superimposition. I also want to do the two steps, translation and scaling, superimposition with semi-landmarks. 

 

Base on what I have read and understood, the semi-landmarks alignment is closely related to the rotation step of the GPA.

Now my question is, can I do the translation and scaling superimposition and sliding of semi-landmarks. If yes, can you suggest how to go about.

 

Once again, thanks for your work in sharing valuable knowledge and I wait any response,

 

Cordially,

 

Angel
